title: Region decider: composite latency + network score and model-fallback matrix
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: implement a region selection component that computes a composite score per region using short-window latency telemetry (p50/p95) and a separate network health signal, then routes requests by tier and falls back to compatible model variants when primary region/tier fails.

Scope: collect streaming p50/p95 per-model-per-region over 10s and 3m windows; ingest network health indicators (packet loss, recent error rates, control-plane heartbeats) normalized to a 0-100 health score; compute a weighted composite (default weights p95:0.5, p50:0.2, network_health:0.3) with smoothing (exponential decay alpha=0.2) and outlier clamping. Use composite thresholds to place regions into routing bands (Preferred / Secondary / Unhealthy).

Routing rules: for requests with latency SLOs (tier=low-latency/high-throughput), consult region band + cost multiplier to pick best region. If the top region has degraded below band/unavailable, consult fallback matrix that prefers compatible model variants (smaller quantized variant or regional replica) respecting model-compatibility metadata. Fallback decisions must preserve safety: only pick a variant with identical API contract and accepted quantization levels.

Observability & testing: add per-region score timeseries in Console (charts for p50,p95,network_health,composite), a simulation harness to replay production traces and measure routing decisions, and end-to-end canary with synthetic traffic. Provide a debug endpoint to show selected region/score rationale for a request id.

Trade-offs discussed: short windows are reactive but noisy; longer windows stabilize decisions but delay fallbacks. We choose dual-window approach (10s react, 3m stable) and require both windows to degrade before moving region to Unhealthy to avoid flapping. Weighting will be configurable per-customer.

Backward compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged unless tenant enables "composite-region-decider" feature flag. Migration: gradual rollout to 10% of hosts then 50% then all.

2026-03-04 - RS: PoC collector implemented that emits p50/p95 and network_health every 10s; initial noise observed around midnight maintenance windows.
2026-03-05 - LH (Design): Console mockups added for composite score heatmap. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/region-heatmap-v2

2026-03-07 - RS: Simulation run against 72h replay (trace id set A) shows 12% fewer cross-region fallbacks vs naive p95-only routing, but 4% higher tail latency on some clients — need tuning of weights.
2026-03-09 - PM (Marcus Li): Customer impact review — medium; enterprise tenants want per-tenant weight overrides and audit logs for fallback decisions.

qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring logic (edge cases, clamping, smoothing). 2) Integration test: ingest synthetic telemetry to validate band transitions. 3) Replay simulation harness to assert fallback matrix correctness. 4) Canary: enable feature flag for 10% of traffic with synthetic latency SLO checks. 5) Load test to ensure scoring computation adds <0.5ms p95 CPU overhead per host.
acceptance_criteria: Composite score produced every 10s and every 3m for every region-model pair
Regions correctly classified into Preferred/Secondary/Unhealthy according to thresholds in config
Routing selects an eligible region and falls back to a compatible model variant when necessary
Console shows composite score timeseries and selected-region rationale for sampled requests
Canary rollout passes without >1% customer-facing error increase and with metrics within configured SLOs
